Jake —

Short answers below to close this out for procurement:

1) Dedicated pool, "fast-warm" policy — typical embeddings ingestion RTO: 2–4 minutes (median ~2:30). This is measured from the failover initiation (control-plane failover signal) to first successful inference call completing under the warm path. We included the per-shard median/95th columns in the CSV.

2) KV timings CSV measurement method — start trigger is the control-plane failover completion timestamp (we mark t=0 when the primary orchestrator signals node reallocation). Endpoints measured: first successful GET latency returning cached KV entry (represents warmed KV), 50/95/99 percentiles across the active shard set, and the observed additional token-generation latency caused by cold KV misses. Column header "trigger_ts" indicates the t=0 marker used.

If you'd like raw logs for the specific windows, we can provide them under the standard MSA/NDA; otherwise the CSV and signed attestation should satisfy procurement. Let me know if procurement needs a brief note for the contract file.

— Soojin
Security & Compliance Liaison
